title: Approve os_mem_alloc_aligned over-allocation alignment repair
summary: The target TODO cannot be retired against the frozen unix_mmapx executable path using only internal proof/spec propagation; unix_mmapx can return a successful mmap pointer with only page-alignment guarantees while callers require alignment up to SEGMENT_SIZE.
rationale: A proof-only attempt added internal alignment postconditions through os_mem_alloc/unix_mmap/unix_mmapx while restoring the frozen unix_mmapx body. Verification failed at both successful unix_mmapx return exits because the sanctioned mmap wrapper contracts do not imply requested-alignment or hint-equality. The concrete os_alloc.rs patch over-allocates by try_alignment and splits the mapped MemChunk to an aligned subrange, which establishes the existing os_mem_alloc_aligned postcondition without changing frozen goal contracts or os_mem.rs.
machine_evidence: Attempt pa-1 first failing VC: os_alloc.rs:321:13 postcondition not satisfied at unix_mmapx returns on lines 350 and 360. With the over-allocation candidate applied, make verify exits 0 with 738 verified/0 errors, boundary_guard and spec_drift pass, proof_state next no longer lists os_mem_alloc_aligned as a direct types.rs::todo caller, literal non-lib todo count is 11, and ast_consistency remains red with 4 mismatches due frozen-exec changes requiring review.
first_failing_vc: os_alloc.rs:321:13 postcondition not satisfied at unix_mmapx successful return exits when proving try_alignment > 1 ==> addr % try_alignment == 0 on the frozen executable path
implementation_inventory: verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs::os_mem_alloc_aligned removes the target todo branch and relies on propagated alignment
verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs::os_mem_alloc and ::unix_mmap propagate an internal alignment postcondition
verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs::unix_mmapx over-allocates for try_alignment > 1, aligns inside the mapping, and splits MemChunk to the returned range
established_facts: The frozen unix_mmapx body returns successful mmap_prot_read_write/mmap_prot_none results directly after an optional hint attempt.
The sanctioned os_mem.rs wrappers do not expose a contract that a successful mmap result equals a nonzero hint or is aligned above page_size.
The applied os_alloc.rs over-allocation patch is the concrete middle-layer behavior change that proves the target postcondition without modifying os_mem.rs or frozen goal contracts.
residual_uncertainty: Operator/reviewer must decide whether this frozen-executable change is acceptable, or whether a separate external mmap contract decision should be made instead.

options.label: overallocate-and-split
options.trade: Changes os_alloc.rs executable behavior for try_alignment > 1; avoids strengthening os_mem.rs and proves the returned MemChunk covers the aligned subrange.

review_reason: Candidate od-1 is semantically earned and now requires operator authority. I independently reran the relevant gates: `make verify` exits 0 with `738 verified, 0 errors`; `boundary_guard` passes with no net TCB growth and frozen goal contracts byte-identical; `spec_drift` is clean for `verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs`; refreshed `proof_state next` reports `os_mem_alloc_aligned@L136` as `in_verification` with no `types.rs::todo@L2210` trust leaf, and the remaining `types.rs::todo` callers are other sites; the non-lib literal `todo();` count is 11. The blockers are exactly the reviewed escalation state: `ast_consistency` remains red with 4 mismatches, and `operator_decisions gate` reports `CANDIDATE_REVIEW` for od-1. Attempt pa-1 records the proof-only frozen-path failure at `os_alloc.rs:321:13`: the frozen `unix_mmapx` can return a successful mmap result directly, while the sanctioned `os_mem.rs` mmap contracts do not guarantee requested alignment or hint equality. Strengthening that bottom boundary is disallowed by this mission, so the currently verified repair depends on an executable over-allocation-and-split change in `os_alloc.rs`, which cannot be accepted silently.
operator_question: Approve od-1: allow the verified `os_alloc.rs` frozen-exec over-allocation-and-split repair in `unix_mmapx` to retire the `os_mem_alloc_aligned` alignment TODO without strengthening `os_mem.rs`?
resolution_note:
REJECTED. The diagnosis in pa-1 is accepted as correct: the sanctioned os_mem.rs mmap contracts guarantee only page alignment, so the os_mem_alloc_aligned postcondition cannot be discharged by internal proof/spec propagation alone. The over-allocation SHAPE is also the right idea. The submitted patch is rejected for three concrete defects, not for its direction.

(1) WRONG PLACEMENT. The patch installs the over-allocation at the top of unix_mmapx and takes it unconditionally whenever try_alignment > 1. The todo() being retired lives in os_mem_alloc_aligned, on the FALLBACK path that is reached only after os_mem_alloc has already returned a pointer and that pointer turned out to be misaligned (p.addr() % alignment != 0). A rare fallback has been turned into the always-taken path: every segment allocation now maps SEGMENT_ALIGN (32 MiB) of extra address space, not just the misaligned ones. Fix the site where the todo() actually is, and only on the misalignment branch.

(2) THE RECLAIM IS FICTIONAL. MemChunk::split is a proof fn (os_mem_util.rs:34). It is pure ghost: it partitions the permission token and has no effect whatsoever on the operating system. After the split the patch returns aligned_mem and drops the remainder, so the head padding and the tail surplus remain mapped in the process address space forever while their permission is discarded and can never be recovered. Splitting a ghost permission is not releasing memory. Whatever you over-allocate, you must actually give back.

(3) BYPASSES THE EXISTING ALIGNMENT MECHANISM. The new branch returns before the hint logic, so os_get_aligned_hint never runs when try_alignment > 1. That path exists precisely to obtain an aligned address on the first attempt. Do not delete a working mechanism and replace it with an unconditional worst case; the fallback must sit behind it, not in front of it.

Standing constraints are unchanged: no net-new trust, no weakening or strengthening of a sanctioned contract to assume a property the underlying syscall does not actually provide, no ensures false, and no substituting one escape hatch for another. Record the outcome of this review and any further failed approaches in research/proof_attempts.jsonl. If after that you conclude that no correct implementation of this fallback is expressible with the operations currently available to the project, say so explicitly in a new candidate, name the exact missing capability and why project code cannot provide it, and let the operator decide.

title: Expose executable partial unmap for os_mem_alloc_aligned fallback
summary: The corrected os_mem_alloc_aligned fallback needs to over-allocate only after a misaligned first allocation and then return head/tail surplus to the OS, but the current project exposes no executable munmap/release primitive to do that.
rationale: The accepted repair shape must run inside the p.addr() % alignment != 0 branch, behind os_get_aligned_hint, and cannot use MemChunk::split or os_restrict as reclamation because they are proof-only. Existing os_mem.rs wrappers expose mmap_prot_read_write, mmap_prot_none, mprotect_prot_read_write, and mprotect_prot_none; mprotect_prot_none preserves os_exact_range and only changes protection, so it cannot remove surplus ranges from the process mapping or from the MemChunk OS domain. Adding a wrapper around libc::munmap/OS release would be a new trusted bottom boundary, which the engineer cannot introduce without operator approval.
machine_evidence: Attempt pa-3: make verify exits 0 with 736 verified, 0 errors; proof_state next still reports verus-mimalloc/types.rs::todo@L2210; project source audit found no munmap/unmap/release implementation, only mprotect and mmap wrappers.
first_failing_vc: n/a: no proof VC can be attempted for a correct fallback because the required executable release operation is absent from the available project API
implementation_inventory: verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs::os_mem_alloc_aligned fallback must unmap the original misaligned allocation and/or any head/tail surplus from a fallback over-allocation before returning an aligned subrange.
verus-mimalloc/os_mem.rs currently has mmap_prot_* and mprotect_prot_* wrappers only; it has no munmap/release wrapper whose contract removes bytes from MemChunk::os and PointsToRaw.
established_facts: The existing hint path remains first: os_mem_alloc calls unix_mmapx, and unix_mmapx attempts os_get_aligned_hint before falling back to an arbitrary successful mmap result.
The existing project-owned operations cannot genuinely give back surplus mapped memory; MemChunk::split/os_restrict are proof-only, and mprotect_prot_none does not unmap or shrink the OS range.
Adding a libc::munmap-backed wrapper with a MemChunk range-consumption contract would be new trusted bottom-boundary surface and is engineer-forbidden under the current no-net-new-trust rule.
residual_uncertainty: Operator/reviewer must decide whether to approve a new sanctioned external release primitive, accept a different runtime behavior for misaligned fallback, or redirect this bounded task to another todo site.
external_dependency: libc::munmap / OS virtual-memory unmap or equivalent release primitive

options.label: add-munmap-release
options.trade: Adds a sanctioned executable release wrapper that consumes exact MemChunk ranges so the fallback can split permissions and actually unmap surplus head/tail pages instead of dropping ghost permissions.

review_reason: Reviewer certifies od-2: the accepted fallback requires real partial unmap/release of mapped surplus, current project APIs expose only mmap/mprotect and proof-only MemChunk splitting/restricting, so adding a munmap-style wrapper is new bottom-boundary trust and requires operator authority.
operator_question: Approve od-2: add a sanctioned executable partial unmap/release primitive (for example libc::munmap) with MemChunk permission accounting, or choose a different acceptable fallback behavior/redirect this bounded task?
resolution_note:
APPROVED WITH A CORRECTED CONTRACT. The capability audit is accepted: mprotect_prot_none preserves os_exact_range and only changes protection, MemChunk::split and os_restrict are proof-only, and no executable release primitive existed. munmap is a real syscall that project code cannot implement, so this is a legitimate new bottom boundary rather than a proof shortcut. The escalation was raised correctly: source left unchanged, patch kept research-only, no sanctioned contract quietly strengthened.

The operator has applied the primitive (commit 47e8db9) and rebaselined; verus-mimalloc/os_mem.rs::munmap_release is now sanctioned TCB. Do NOT add it yourself, it is already there.

THE PROPOSED CONTRACT WAS INCOMPLETE AND WAS FIXED BEFORE LANDING. Your version constrained only the OS side: wf() is defined as wf_os(), and os_exact_range pins only os.dom(), so points_to.dom() was left entirely free. A caller could therefore split the PointsToRaw for those bytes out of the chunk, retain it, hand in a chunk carrying only the OS range, and then write through the retained permission after the pages were unmapped. That is a use-after-free the verifier would have accepted. The landed contract adds has_pointsto_for_all_read_write(), exactly as mprotect_prot_none (os_mem.rs) already requires it, which forces every read-write page's byte permission to be surrendered with the chunk. Note that the stronger form 'points_to.dom() covers the whole range' would have been WRONG in the other direction: mmap_prot_none produces no pointsto at all, so prot_none chunks could never satisfy it, and the !request_commit path needs to release those. Study the landed signature before you call it.

GENERAL LESSON, apply it to every future boundary you propose: when you write a trusted contract, the danger is not only an ensures that promises more than the syscall delivers, but equally a requires that demands less than soundness needs. Enumerate every resource the operation destroys and require that ALL of it is surrendered.

NOW IMPLEMENT THE FALLBACK, at verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs where the todo() actually is, inside the p.addr() % alignment != 0 branch, behind os_get_aligned_hint. You now hold a real release primitive, so there is no excuse for a ghost-only reclaim: the misaligned mapping you already obtained must itself be munmap_release'd rather than dropped, and after over-allocating and splitting out the aligned subrange, the head and tail surplus must be genuinely released too. Every byte you map and do not return must end up in the pointer you hand back. make verify must stay at 0 errors. Record any further materially distinct failed approach in research/proof_attempts.jsonl.

title: Sanction vendored Verus builtin/vstd primitives as bottom TCB
summary: completion_gate is red only because rust-analyzer traverses vendored Verus builtin/vstd path dependencies that are outside the project-owned source root but currently lack sanctioned path rules.
rationale: The frozen tcb_baseline source roots scan verus-mimalloc only, while Cargo.toml includes .verus_deps/builtin and .verus_deps/vstd as workspace members so rust-analyzer can resolve macros and path dependencies. proof_state therefore registers reachable dependency functions but cannot classify them from scanned project source facts, leaving 15 unknown nodes. Actual source inspection shows the nodes are Verus/vstd primitives or external_body/axiom wrappers, not project-owned functions whose middle-layer proof can be supplied. A temporary baseline copy with tcb_manifest path rules for .verus_deps/builtin and .verus_deps/vstd closes completion_gate without changing allocator source.
machine_evidence: make verify exits 0 with 759 verified, 0 errors. Current completion_gate exits 1 with exactly 15 reachable unknown nodes under .verus_deps/builtin and .verus_deps/vstd. Simulated tcb_manifest path rules for those two dependency roots make completion_gate PASS.
first_failing_vc: n/a: source-derived completion gate obligation, not an SMT VC; unknown nodes are outside verus-mimalloc source roots and are Verus/vstd trusted primitive boundaries
implementation_inventory: .verus_deps/builtin/src/lib.rs::Ghost::assume_new_fallback and Tracked::assume_new/assume_new_fallback are Verus builtin erasure constructors reached from many verified project call paths.

.verus_deps/vstd/atomic_ghost.rs::new, cell/pcell.rs::{new,borrow,borrow_mut}, layout.rs::layout_for_type_is_valid, and raw_ptr.rs::{expose_provenance,ptr_mut_read,ptr_mut_ref,ptr_mut_write,ptr_ref,with_exposed_provenance} are vendored vstd primitives reached by heap_init/heap_malloc/free callers.

The project-owned real call paths are already verified by make verify; the remaining nodes live outside the tcb_baseline src_roots and cannot be discharged by adding allocator middle-layer invariants or lemmas.
established_facts: proof_state summary after refresh: 194 reachable functions, 527 edges, 0 WIP trust, 0 unentered, 15 unknown, 0 unmapped trust, 2 unreachable informational trust leaves.

Every unknown node path starts with .verus_deps/builtin or .verus_deps/vstd; representative sources carry verifier external/external_body/axiom primitives for ghost construction, permissioned cells, layouts, raw pointers, and atomic ghost state.

Using the existing tcb_manifest path-rule mechanism in a throwaway baseline copy with .verus_deps/builtin and .verus_deps/vstd makes completion_gate report PASS, showing this is a boundary classification issue rather than a project proof obligation.
residual_uncertainty: Reviewer/operator must decide whether the broad dependency-root sanction is the intended local policy, or whether the gate should instead hard-code Verus toolchain dependency handling outside the project TCB manifest.
external_dependency: Verus builtin/vstd trusted primitive implementation boundary vendored under .verus_deps

options.label: manifest-path-rules
options.trade: Operator-owned TCB-manifest update that sanctions the vendored Verus builtin/vstd dependency roots; in a throwaway baseline copy this exact rule shape made completion_gate PASS.

review_reason: Reviewer certifies od-3: make verify is green at 759 verified/0 errors; boundary_guard is green with no net TCB growth; proof_state/completion_gate show the only unresolved reachable obligations are 15 unknown nodes rooted under .verus_deps/builtin and .verus_deps/vstd; those sources are Verus builtin/vstd primitive boundaries with external_body/axiom/uninterp behavior outside the project source roots, and pa-5 plus the throwaway manifest-path test show the existing project-local closure mechanism is operator-owned tcb_manifest sanctioning rather than middle-layer allocator proof work.
operator_question: Approve od-3: sanction .verus_deps/builtin and .verus_deps/vstd in .verus_agent/tcb_manifest.json as the vendored Verus/vstd bottom/toolchain TCB, or require a tool-level policy change instead?
resolution_note:
APPROVED as filed, option=manifest-path-rules; operator applied and committed it in 00fb4e2 (agents must not edit tcb_manifest.json).

Your diagnosis was right and the discipline was right: you did not touch allocator source, you did not try to 'prove' a vstd axiom, and you did not paper over it with a local external_body. You escalated a boundary-classification question to the boundary owner. That is exactly the correct move.

Reasoning: .verus_deps/{builtin,vstd} is the Verus standard library, vendored only so rust-analyzer can resolve macros and path deps for the cargo view. It sits BELOW the project at the same trust level as the Verus compiler and the SMT solver. It is not TCB growth -- it was always trusted; the frozen tcb_baseline just scanned verus-mimalloc/ and never classified it. Nothing you could have written in the crate would discharge Tracked::assume_new or the raw_ptr axioms.

What made this safe to approve, and what you should have stated yourself: a path-rule sanction over a directory is only sound if that directory is pristine. Operator checked it -- every .rs under .verus_deps is byte-identical to verus-lang/verus @1847ab36, and no commit after the scaffolding freeze touched it. Had the agent edited even one line there, this sanction would have laundered those edits into the trusted base. GENERAL LESSON: whenever you propose sanctioning a PATH rather than a named symbol, you inherit everything currently in that path AND everything later added to it. Ship the provenance evidence (upstream diff + git log of the directory) with the request; do not make the operator go find it.

Mission status is now: make verify 759 verified / 0 errors, todo() outside lib.rs == 0, completion_gate PASS, net-new trust in verus-mimalloc == the single operator-authored munmap_release from od-2. That is the completion criterion met. Assemble the evidence bundle.

title: RETROACTIVE operator ratification: page-alignment ensures on mmap_prot_none
summary: Agent added 'pt.0 as int % page_size() == 0' to the ensures of mmap_prot_none in the sanctioned-TCB file os_mem.rs WITHOUT filing an operator decision. Strengthening the contract of a trusted external_body function is operator-owned. Operator ratifies the fact but flags the process violation.
rationale: The postcondition is TRUE of the underlying syscall: POSIX requires mmap to return a page-aligned address, and the sister function mmap_prot_read_write already carries the identical ensures. The asymmetry was an upstream omission, not a deliberate weakening. Operator had independently reached the same conclusion and would have approved this had it been filed.
machine_evidence: See pa-6: deleting the single line takes make verify from 759 verified/0 errors to 758 verified/1 error. The proof genuinely relies on it. boundary_guard reports PASS both with and without the line.
established_facts: The added ensures is load-bearing: removing it yields 758 verified / 1 error.
mmap_prot_read_write already carries the identical page-alignment ensures; mmap_prot_none lacking it was an upstream asymmetry.
boundary_guard PASSes in both states, so the harness cannot detect contract strengthening inside an already-sanctioned file.
residual_uncertainty: Process: agent must not silently edit sanctioned TCB contracts. Harness: boundary_guard counts trust MARKERS but does not hash contract TEXT of sanctioned-TCB functions, so this change class is invisible to it.

options.label: as-landed
options.trade: True of POSIX mmap and symmetric with mmap_prot_read_write; cost is that it was landed without operator review

resolution_note:
RATIFIED AS LANDED by operator. The postcondition stays. But read this carefully, because the process failure matters more than the line.

WHAT HAPPENED: you added 'pt.0 as int % page_size() == 0' to the ensures of mmap_prot_none in verus-mimalloc/os_mem.rs and shipped it in a [verus][argus] commit with no operator decision filed. os_mem.rs is sanctioned permanent TCB. Sanctioned means its trust is ACCEPTED, not that its contracts are YOURS to edit. Every ensures on an external_body function is an unproved promise about the outside world that the whole proof rests on; adding one enlarges what the artifact trusts just as surely as adding a new external_body would. That is an operator decision, always, even when the fact is obvious.

WHY IT IS RATIFIED ANYWAY: the claim is true. POSIX requires mmap to return a page-aligned address, and mmap_prot_read_write in the very same file already carried the identical ensures -- mmap_prot_none lacking it was an upstream asymmetry, not a deliberate weakening. Had you filed it, operator would have approved it; operator had in fact independently reached the same conclusion. Reverting a true postcondition to punish the procedure would be theater.

WHAT YOU SHOULD HAVE DONE: file the decision, cite the sister function as precedent, cite POSIX, show the failing VC, and keep working on something else until it resolved. You did exactly that for od-2 and od-3 and it worked well both times. This one you skipped, and the likely reason is that it felt too small and too obviously true to be worth a gate. That instinct is the thing to distrust. 'Obviously true of the syscall' is precisely the reasoning that also justifies a WRONG ensures -- it is the same sentence an unsound change would come wrapped in. The operator gate exists so that the judgement of 'obviously true' is made by the party that owns the consequences.

HARNESS NOTE, NOT YOUR FAULT: operator verified boundary_guard PASSes both with and without your line. It counts trust MARKERS and hashes frozen top-spec files; it does not hash the contract TEXT of already-sanctioned TCB functions. So nothing would have caught this but self-discipline. Do not read that gap as permission. Going forward, treat any edit to a requires/ensures inside a sanctioned-TCB file as gated even though the tooling will let it through silently, and say so explicitly in your evidence bundle.

FOR THE BUNDLE: disclose this episode yourself, in the trust section, in these terms -- one contract strengthening in sanctioned TCB, landed without a gate, retroactively ratified as od-4, load-bearing per pa-6. An evidence bundle that omits it is not honest, and operator will check.
